Welcome

A note from Ayis & Lucas

Dear Guest,

Welcome to the Rustic Retreat, and thank you for choosing our cabin! We're two brothers, Ayis and Lucas; we grew up in Miami and now live in New York and Chicago. We fought and argued a lot growing up, but decided to buy a cabin together anyway, as a place to bring friends and family. We picked the Great Smoky Mountains for its proximity and because we both love being outdoors.

Over the years we've put blood (mostly splinters), sweat, and tears into this place. Our goal was to build a beautiful, inviting space where everyone can enjoy everything this area has to offer; we hope that shows in your stay. As we keep improving our hands on skills, we're always working to make the cabin better, so if you have suggestions, we'd genuinely love to hear them.

We hope you have a fun, relaxing, and above all safe stay. Messaging us through the app is the fastest way to reach us.

✦ Meet Your Hosts
Lucas
Vegan. Once ate two Chipotle bowls in one sitting. Fractured his skull pulling Ayis up a boat.
Ayis
Has a twin brother (not Lucas). Dim sum is his favorite meal. Claims he's better at soccer than Lucas.
✦ Getting Here

Google and Apple Maps both work well, but you'll lose signal in the mountains; start your route before you lose service so it keeps navigating. Some roads have steep inclines, but the conditions aren't scary and a normal sedan is fine; 4WD isn't necessary. If you're driving at night, go slowly, since most roads aren't well lit.

You'll pass one driveway, then a smaller one that leads right to the cabin. Park anywhere along either; there's plenty of room. Most guests find it easiest to park at the very top, right next to the stairs.

📓
Look for the blue Experience Notebook in the cabin: leave a note about your stay, favorite restaurants, or things you got up to. Future guests (and we) love reading them!

Check in and check out times are strictly enforced. On turnover days, that 5 hour window is what lets us get the place ready for the next friends staying with us. If you do run past the grace period, a $100 late fee applies, plus $100 for each additional hour. Thanks for helping us keep it running smoothly!

✦ Address

1357 Pine Trail, Sevierville, TN 37876

Heads up: depending on carrier, cell signal may be spotty on the way in, so it's worth starting your GPS route before you lose coverage, so it keeps navigating.

✦ Checking In

The cabin uses an electronic lock. Your access code was sent in your welcome message. Enter the code, wait for the checkmark and confirmation chime, then open the door. The door fits snug, so you may need to push a little harder than expected.

✦ Checking Out
  1. Leave the laundry to us: bed as is, towels on the first floor bathroom floor.
  2. Please start the dishwasher for any unwashed dishes before leaving.
  3. Remove all items from the refrigerator and place all trash bags in the basement: please knot the bags (this keeps bears away; see the Bear Safety section). The basement lock code is 2652. Enter through the double doors at the top of the driveway, or once you go down the exterior stairs, turn right.
  4. Make sure all the lights are turned off, windows closed, doors locked, and everything is back in its place.
  5. Drive safely!
🔒
Always lock the cabin and car doors. Bears have a sense of smell far better than a dog's and have opened unlocked car doors or climbed through open sunroofs to get to food inside; this has happened here before.
🤝

Safety & Evacuation

Please read before your first night
🚨
In any emergency, call 911 immediately. The cabin address is 1357 Pine Trail, Sevierville, TN 37876.
✦ Fire Extinguishers

There are three fire extinguishers in the cabin. All closets containing a fire extinguisher have a "Fire Extinguisher Inside" sticker on their door.

  • Basement: on the left side once you walk in
  • First floor: underneath the kitchen sink
  • Loft: at the top of the staircase
✦ Detectors & First Aid

Every bedroom has a smoke detector, and the kitchen has a combined smoke/carbon monoxide detector. The first aid kit is located under the kitchen sink and includes bandages, antibiotic ointment, antiseptic towelettes, burn cream, pain relievers, gauze, wound closures, a cold pack, and other essentials.

Bear Safety

You're in black bear country: here's how to stay safe
🐾
Bears have been seen at this cabin before. Please take these steps seriously: never leave food in your car, always lock car doors, and never leave food or trash out on the deck.

The Smoky Mountains are home to American black bears, one of the largest predators in the park, though the vast majority of their diet is actually berries, nuts, and plants. According to the National Park Service, black bears are highly intelligent and can identify food by both smell and sight, not just scent.

✦ Why This Matters

Bears that get into human food or trash quickly lose their natural fear of people and start associating cars, coolers, and cabins with an easy meal. These "food conditioned" bears become more dangerous to guests and, sadly, are often the ones that end up euthanized. Keeping food secured protects both you and the bears.

✦ At the Cabin
  • Lock your car doors at all times: bears can open unlocked doors or climb through a cracked window or open sunroof, and have done so here before.
  • Never leave food, coolers, or scented items in your car: this includes drinks, snacks, sunscreen, and toiletries, not just meals.
  • Keep all food inside the cabin with doors and windows closed when you're not in the room, since bears can push through an open door or window.
  • Nothing food related on the deck: no coolers, food left out, or trash bags, even briefly.
  • Knot all trash bags before placing them in the basement can: loose bags attract bears through smell far more than sealed ones.
  • Wash dirty dishes promptly rather than leaving them out overnight.
👀
If you do spot a bear from a distance, enjoy the moment from inside; do not approach, feed, or try to photograph it up close. Learn more from the NPS black bear safety page.
♨️

Hot Tub

One of everyone's favorite parts of the stay
🔞
Hot tub use is for guests 25 and over only, and is at your own risk. No alcohol or drugs at or near the hot tub; heat speeds up their effects and can cause unconsciousness.
  • If you've been drinking, we recommend skipping the hot tub; leave immediately if you feel uncomfortable or sleepy.
  • You sweat out fluids in the water without noticing, so stay extra hydrated.
  • Always cover the hot tub when not in use, to prevent accidental drowning, preserve water temperature, and maintain cleanliness.
  • The tub is emptied and cleaned after every guest, so if you use it shortly after check in, it may still be warming up.
✦ Jets

Press the jet button to turn the jets on. Turn the knobs on either side of the control panel to adjust jet speed.

✦ Temperature

Press the temperature button repeatedly to cycle to your desired setting, between 80 to 104°F. Current temperature shows on the panel screen.

✦ Lights

Press "Light" once to turn lights on, again to turn off, and a third time to turn back on in a new color. Repeated presses cycle through red, blue, green, purple, light blue, light green, and turquoise.

Technology

Wifi, fireplace, thermostat, TVs
✦ Wifi
Network
RusticRetreat
Password
EnjoyYourStay!

The modem and router are located below the TV in the living room.

✦ Fireplace

The fireplace is a small electric device, we converted it due to safety and wildfire risk; just grab the remote to control it. It has both a heater and a traditional flame feature.

Heater: Press the Heater button to turn it on. You can set a timer for it to power on or off (options: 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, or off): press the Timer button repeatedly to cycle through options. The power off timer only works while the heater is on; the power on timer only works while it's off.

Flame: Press the Flame button to turn the (electronic) flame on or off.

✦ Thermostat

Located on the living room wall, right outside the master bedroom.

✦ TVs

Each bedroom has a Roku TV with guest mode (use HDMI 1 for the upstairs bedrooms). Enter your checkout date when you first turn it on, and the TV handles the rest automatically, including logging you out at the time of checkout!

✦ Locking Up

Unlock: enter your code, wait for the checkmark and chime, open the door.
Lock: close the door and press the lock button on the bottom right.

Cabin Improvements

A look at what's changed over the years

We love visiting the area with friends and family, so when we can, we try to improve the cabin to make it feel more homey. Here's a look at some of the bigger projects we're proud of.

Kitchen Renovation 2025

We rebuilt the kitchen with new hickory cabinetry, quartz counters, a green herringbone tile backsplash, and updated stainless appliances, while keeping the original stacked stone fireplace and hand hewn beams that give the cabin its character.

Local Recommendations

Things to do, eat, and shop nearby

The cabin is centrally located to all the top attractions: Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Dollywood, Anakeesta, and The Island: just a quick 10 to 15 minute drive to both Gatlinburg and Pigeon Forge.

🎢 Dollywood · 10 to 15 min 🥾 Smokies trailheads · 10 to 20 min 🛍️ The Parkway strip · 10 to 15 min
